issues.description: The release lacks both profile CSVs. The documented 2014/2016 Recruiter history does not verify a current compatible export, exact CSV headers, key consistency, or complete job/education-history coverage; no access barrier was established.

The cleaned profile directory and text key-to-state adoption crosswalk are not produced or packaged. The appendix provides a jurisdiction/effective-date table that can inform the separate state-level State_Adoptions lookup, but exact state-label normalization, the directory fields/route, and the profile-key-to-state_id mapping remain unresolved. The source programs expect these files under different roots.

Local catalog candidates match the required Audit Analytics auditor key/name, Compustat gvkey/conm/fyear and CRSP permno/comnam fields and passed one-row reads. The author's dated roster vintages, population, periods and identifier semantics remain unverified, so these are not verified substitutes.

No supplied source creates Desc_Complex.dta or computes the consumed fog_index, flesch_score, num_words and num_sentences fields. Appendix formulas document Fog/Flesch definitions, but do not establish the author scoring implementation or the prepared field units/missingness.

The text branch reads separate 2_Data paths for the directory, Adoption_Linking_File, working_ind_full and ind_emp_sum. The CPA producers write temp/working_ind_full and output/Ind_Emp_Sum under another root/case; no copy, key/schema check, or CWD configuration establishes those as the same inputs.

The independent NASBA branch's university-level DTA is absent. The datasheet documents historical public-PDF digitization and the code mentions contacting NASBA, but current official URLs, delivery, exact fields and year/university coverage remain unverified; there is no access-barrier proof.

The NASBA program labels log_Cand, Rule_150, Int_150, and yearb1, later generates log_cand and Rule_1, and drops/recreates Int_150. Stata treats log_Cand and log_cand as distinct variable names; the unseen input's actual variables and the intended relationship of Rule_150 to Rule_1 and the other labeled variables remain unknown. Confirm the input schema and author intent before running; do not invent an alias or repair.

Clean Raw Data destrings end_year at line 64, then performs string replacements and egen sieve(end_year) through line 107, and destrings again at line 109. The early conversion conflicts with the intervening string operations. A supported preparation edit removes the duplicate early conversion so the existing final conversion follows the string cleanup.

The foreach statement at line 1468 uses varlis rather than the varlist keyword used by nearby foreach statements. The source correction is a mechanical token repair with no change to the listed variables.

The working-data driver ends multiple continued statements/lists with single // and starts the next line with a bare operator or field. These markers terminate the prior line as comments. Changing only those markers to /// preserves the authored conditions and lists.

The Compustat roster is split into 0..40000 ID chunks, but the match-result producer loop covers only 28000..40000; a later merge loop requests tempfile macros for 0..40000 although only 28000..40000 were created. The intended match coverage and correct final loop bounds require clarification; no chunk range or sample restriction is guessed.

The code initializes and aggregates long_tenure_check but line 274 replaces long_tenure. Without the experience CSV schema this may be a missing input field or a misdirected source assignment; confirm whether long_tenure exists and the intended check target before changing it.

actions.description: After input, software, CWD, and source issues are resolved, execute the supplied preparation branches in their supported producer order while keeping textual and NASBA inputs distinct.
steps: Use a CPA_Profile_Sample working copy as the current directory, create its referenced raw, temp, output, and check directories, and stage the compatible profile, lookup, and company-roster inputs.
After resolving the listed source and software requirements, run 1_Clean_Raw_Data.do first; it produces Experience_Clean, Title_Clean, Company_Clean, Ind_Emp_Sum, and Education_Clean.

Run 2_Build_Working_Data.do second from the same CPA working directory; it consumes the cleaning outputs plus the cleaned directory and state-level adoption lookup and produces working_individual_data and its CEM output.

Run the textual Build_Working_Data.do third only from the author-confirmed working directory after Desc_Complex.dta and the separate 2_Data/input and 2_Data/temp handoffs are staged and schema-checked; it produces 2_Data/output/Desc_clean.

Run NASBA_Supply_Sample/Build_Working_Data.do as its own branch from its confirmed NASBA working directory after the prepared NASBA input and source namespace are resolved; it produces output/workingdata.dta.
validation: Before each future run, verify the exact current directory and required input/output directory names because none of the four programs supplies an explicit cd command.
After each branch, verify the named source outputs exist and the next branch's key names, types, and case-specific paths match its documented handoff; do not run text preparation before CPA stage 2.
No regression/estimation driver or compatible analysis-data route is supplied in this package; this proposal covers the four supplied preparation programs only.

review_notes: Static review covers the datasheet, appendix, and all four supplied Stata programs. No author program, import, estimation, data transformation, or syntax trial was run.

The scope keeps CPA profile cleaning first, CPA working-data/CEM construction second, textual-metrics preparation third with its separate 2_Data inputs, and the independent NASBA supply branch distinct. Appendix Figure 6 analysis is contextual because no corresponding analysis program or compatible analysis-data route is supplied.

All 33 frozen dependency IDs are individually reviewed from the source-based producer/consumer trace in probes/workflow_trace.json. Catalog-listed SAS candidates passed bounded row_limit=1 metadata reads, but their author-vintage and population compatibility remains unverified.

The appendix provides a packaged jurisdiction/effective-date adoption table; its conversion to the author's exact state labels remains unverified. The text branch's Adoption_Linking_File is a separate unresolved profile-key crosswalk.

Stata's which token_soundex result is preserved as a check of the option name, not as a missing standalone command: the matchit author documentation identifies token_soundex as a built-in similmethod().

The NASBA source's log_Cand and log_cand spellings are distinct Stata variable names; the uncertainty is the unseen input schema and source intent for labels, Rule_150 versus Rule_1, and the actual Int_150 drop/recreation.
